input.reply:
Thanks for the report. This looks like expected npm peer-dependency behavior rather than a Vitest bug. I couldn't run searches or read the repo here, so this is based on your log.

`vitest`, `@vitest/browser-*` and `@vitest/coverage-*` declare exact-version peer dependencies on each other. For example, `vitest@4.0.2` has an optional peer on `@vitest/browser-playwright@4.0.2`. Your lockfile still pins 4.0.2 for some of them, so bumping one package at a time conflicts. npm reports ERESOLVE.

Update every Vitest package in one command so npm resolves them together:

```bash
npm i -D vitest@4.0.3 @vitest/browser-playwright@4.0.3 @vitest/coverage-v8@4.0.3
```

You should also check that `@vitest/eslint-plugin` isn't pulling in an older `vitest` through its own peer range. In your log it appears in the conflicting tree.

If this still fails with all packages bumped together, please share a minimal repro (a repo or StackBlitz) with the full `npm ls vitest` output.
